body.translated_text: The Teaching on the Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action (<s>Daśākuśalakarmapathadeśanā</s>)

body.text: kenacit sugatiprāptukāmena heyā daśākuśalakarmapathāḥ prakṛtisāvadyāḥ, tadyathā-
body.translated_text: For someone who wishes to attain a fortunate rebirth (<s>sugati</s>), the ten unwholesome courses of action (<s>daśākuśalakarmapathā</s>) — which are blameworthy by nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>) — are to be abandoned. They are as follows:

children.translated_text: "Threefold is the bodily action (<s>kāyikakarma</s>), and fourfold the verbal (<s>vācika</s>);
the mental is of three kinds — these ten are considered the unwholesome ones. // 1 //

body.text: ete pravibhāgaśaḥ vyākhyāyante- tatra tāvat kāyikam-prāṇātipātaḥ, adattādānam, kāmamithyācāraśceti / vācikam- mṛṣāvādaḥ, paiśunyam, pāruṣyam, saṃbhinnapralāpaśca / mānasañca- abhidhyā, vyāpādo, mithyādṛṣṭiśca / tatra prāṇātipātastu prāṇibhāvaḥ, prāṇisaṃjñābhāvaḥ, vadhakacittopasthitiḥ, etadupāyakaraṇam, prāṇāvarodhabhāvaśceti etatpañcāṅgaiḥ saṃyukto bhavati prāṇātipātaḥ /
body.translated_text: These are explained in detail: among these, the bodily [actions] are: killing living beings (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), and sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>). The verbal [actions] are: false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), divisive speech (<s>paiśunya</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), and idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>). The mental [actions] are: covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), ill will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). Among these, killing living beings (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) consists of five factors: the existence of a living being (<s>prāṇibhāva</s>), the cognition that it is a living being (<s>prāṇisaṃjñābhāva</s>), the arising of the mind intent on killing (<s>vadhakacittopasthiti</s>), the application of means for that [purpose] (<s>etadupāyakaraṇa</s>), and the occurrence of the obstruction of breath (<s>prāṇāvarodhabhāva</s>) — killing is associated with these five factors.

body.text: tatra katamat adattādānam? parabhāvaḥ, paraparigrahasaṃjñatvam ca, steyacittopasthitiḥ, tadupāyakaraṇam, sthānacyutiśca etatpañcāṅgasaṃyuktaṃ bhavatyadattādānam /
body.translated_text: What, among these, is taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>)? It consists of [the following] five factors: [the object] belonging to another (<s>parabhāva</s>), the cognition that it is another's possession (<s>paraparigrahasaṃjñatva</s>), the arising of the mind intent on theft (<s>steyacittopasthiti</s>), the application of means for that (<s>tadupāyakaraṇa</s>), and displacement from its location (<s>sthānacyuti</s>) — taking what is not given is associated with these five factors.

body.text: kāmamithyācārastu caturvidhaḥ / asthānam, akālaḥ, adeśaḥ, agamyaśceti / tatra asthānaṃ tu saddharma-pratimādi-bodhisattvasthānācāryopādhyāyadakṣiṇīya- mātā-pitṛ-gurvādisaṃnidhiḥ / akāla iti divase ṛtumatī-garbhiṇī-śiśupoṣiṇībhiḥ anicchāduḥkhadaurmanasyapīḍitābhiḥ, aṣṭāṅgoposathāvasthitau ca / adeśa iti mukhavarcomārgatvaṃ, kumārakanyayoḥ puraḥpṛṣṭharandhratvaṃ svagastatvaṃ ca / agamyāstu sarvāḥ parastriyaḥ dharma-dhvaja-kula-rakṣitāḥ, rājarakṣitāḥ, paraparigṛhītā veśyāḥ, sambandhinyaḥ, tiraścyaśca / evaṃ svabhāryāsevane 'pi bhavati kāmamithyācāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) is of four kinds: wrong place (<s>asthāna</s>), wrong time (<s>akāla</s>), wrong location [of the body] (<s>adeśa</s>), and wrong partner (<s>agamya</s>). Among these, 'wrong place' means [in the] proximity of a place where the true <s>Dharma</s> is upheld — such as an image [of the Buddha], a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s station, the presence of an <s>ācārya</s>, preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), worthy recipient (<s>dakṣiṇīya</s>), mother, father, or teacher and the like. 'Wrong time' means [intercourse] by day, or with a woman in her fertile period, or pregnant, or nursing an infant, or afflicted by unwillingness, pain, or depression, or when [one is] abiding in the eight-limbed observance (<s>aṣṭāṅgaupasatha</s>). 'Wrong location [of the body]' means the mouth, the excretory passage, or the front, back, or side openings of a boy or girl, or one's own body. 'Wrong partners' are: all women belonging to another — whether protected by [their] <s>Dharma</s>, banner, family; or protected by the king; or courtesans contracted by another; or female relatives; and female animals. Even in the use of one's own wife, sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) can occur [in these circumstances].

body.text: tatra mṛṣāvādastu avāstavikatvam, vastusthiticyutiḥ, mithyāsaṃjñābhāvaḥ, mithyopāyopasthitiśca, tadupāyakaraṇanceti mithyāvacanoktiśca ityetat pañcāṅgasaṃyoge mṛṣāvādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Among these, false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>) — consisting of five factors: falseness [of the content] (<s>avāstavakatva</s>), deviation from the actual state of affairs (<s>vastusthitacyuti</s>), the presence of a wrong notion (<s>mithyāsaṃjñābhāva</s>), the arising of the wrong means [to convey it] (<s>mithyopāyopasthiti</s>), the application of means for that (<s>tadupāyakaraṇa</s>), and the utterance of the false statement — false speech is [complete] when these five factors are combined.

body.text: paiśunyaṃ tu kliṣṭacittena parabhedakathanam / pāruṣyamiti paramarmavedhi dveṣavacanam / sambhinnapralāpa iti-rāgopayuktatvād āsaktiyogād vā avācyavacanam / abhidhyeti paradhana-dravyaiśvaryeṣu tīvrāsaktacittatā / vyāpādastu sattveṣu vidveṣabhāvaḥ, etān sattvān haniṣyāmi rotsyāmi, tāḍayiṣyāmi, bandhayiṣyāmi iti cintanam /
body.translated_text: Divisive speech (<s>paiśunya</s>) is telling tales to create division between others, with an afflicted mind. Harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is speech that strikes at the tender parts of another out of hatred. Idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>) is speaking what ought not to be said, on account of attachment or through the bond of craving. Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is an intensely attached mental state directed toward the wealth, possessions, and lordship of others. Ill will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) is a state of hostility toward beings — thinking: 'I will harm, destroy, beat, or bind these beings.'

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭiriti nāsti dānam, na yajñaṃ, nehalokaḥ, na paralokaḥ, na śramaṇaḥ, na brāhmaṇaḥ, na devaḥ, na buddho bhagavān, na arhan, na pratyekabuddhaḥ, na sucaritam na ca duścaritam, na sukṛta-duṣkṛta-karmāṇāṃ phalavipākaśceti /
body.translated_text: Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is [the belief that]: there is no gift (<s>dāna</s>), no sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), no this world (<s>ihaloka</s>), no other world (<s>paraloka</s>), no <s>śramaṇa</s>, no <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, no deity (<s>deva</s>), no <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, no <s>arhat</s>, no <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, no good conduct and no bad conduct, no ripening of the fruit (<s>phalavipāka</s>) of meritorious and demeritorious actions.

body.text: bhagavatā ukte 'āryasaddharmasmṛtyupasthāne' mahāyānasūtre ca nirdiṣṭo daśākuśalakarmapatho 'yaṃ tu mahānarakahetuḥ / daśākuśalakarmapathasevanena patanti sattvā narakeṣu /
body.translated_text: This course of the ten unwholesome actions (<s>daśākuśalakarmapatha</s>), as stated by the <s>Bhagavat</s> in the Mahāyāna sūtra 'The Noble Establishment of Mindfulness of the True <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>Āryasaddharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>), is the cause of the great hells. Through the practice of the ten unwholesome courses of action, beings fall into the hells.
The Teaching on the Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action (<s>Daśākuśalakarmapathadeśanā</s>), composed by the great master's feet <s>Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna</s>, is complete.

body.text: tenaiva bhāratīyopādhyāyena mahāsaṃśodhakalokakṣuṣā bhikṣu-jayaśīlena cānūditaḥ sampāditaśca //
body.translated_text: This was translated and revised by that same Indian master (<s>bhāratīyopādhyāya</s>), the great proofreader and light of the world (<s>mahāsaṃśodhaka-lokakṣus</s>), the monk <s>Jayaśīla</s>.
